history.dynasty: Travancore; legendary origins attributed to the sage Divakara Muni; present structure largely built by Marthanda Varma of Travancore in the 18th century
history.period: Origins claimed to date to the 8th century (also referenced in Skanda Purana and Padma Purana, and counted among the seven Parasurama Kshetras); current architecture 18th century; one of the 108 Divya Desams
history.summary: The Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple inside the East Fort of Thiruvananthapuram is dedicated to Vishnu as Padmanabha, reclining in eternal sleep on the hooded serpent Anantha - an 18-foot idol of 12,008 salagramams from the Gandaki river, viewed through three sanctum doors. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams sung by the Tamil Alvars, and the capital city takes its name from the deity ('Thiruvananthapuram' = the land of Sree Anantha Padmanabhaswamy). The present Kerala-Dravidian structure is largely the work of Marthanda Varma, who in 1750 dedicated the kingdom of Travancore to the deity (Thripadidanam) and ruled as 'Padmanabha Dasa' (servant of Padmanabha). In 2011 the opening of subterranean vaults revealed treasures estimated in billions of dollars, making it famous as the world's richest temple. It remains managed by a trust linked to the Travancore royal family; entry is restricted to Hindus with a strict dress code (men in mundu/dhoti without shirt; women in sari or equivalent).

name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
town_description: Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) is the capital of Kerala, a coastal city built on seven hills at the state's southwestern tip. It is a historic administrative and cultural centre - seat of the Travancore royal family, major museums, the Kerala legislature, and the Technopark IT hub - as well as a beach destination (Kovalam, Varkala nearby). The old city around the East Fort preserves the temple quarter of the Travancore kingdom, with the Padmanabhaswamy Temple at its heart.

travel.road: Inside the East Fort; city buses and autos; the temple is adjacent to Pazhavangadi Ganapathy Temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; festival periods (Navaratri, Alpashi/Panguni Utsavam) draw the largest crowds
